report.source_text: On the H&E-stained slides, a 4 mm tumour was found in the dermis. The tumour had a solid pattern in the centre and a more organoid pattern without any necrosis or mucin in the border of the tumour, deeper in the dermis (figure 1A). The tumour cells were fairly uniform with oval to round nuclei with dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and eosinophilic and fine granular cytoplasm (figure 1B). The mitotic counts were 8 per 2 mm2.

report.source_text: The immunohistochemical staining was positive in the peripheral part of the tumour for synaptophysin, CD56, S-100 and SOX-10, special AT-rich sequence-binding protein 2 (SATB2), ISLET-1 and dot-like positive stain for pan cytokeratin (AE1/AE3). The centre of the tumour stained negative for synaptophysin but was partly positive for CD56, S-100 and SOX-10. Staining was negative for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), cytokeratin 20 (CK20), thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1), melanoma antigen (Melan A), chromogranin A, CDX-2, serotonin, melanoma-specific antigen (MSA), microphthalmia transcription factor (MITF), CD45, CD3 and CD20. clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his late 30s presented with a 4 mm skin tumor under his left nipple, present for 5-6 years. Initial excision revealed a dermal tumor with solid and organoid patterns, uniform cells, and a mitotic count of 8 per 2 mm2 (E001). Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, CD56) and markers consistent with cutaneous origin (S-100, SOX-10, SATB2, ISLET-1, dot-like pan cytokeratin), while being negative for Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV), CK20, TTF-1, and Melan A. The Ki-67 index was up to 10% (E002). Post-excision imaging included a negative FDG-PET and a Gallium-PET that highlighted two non-malignant birthmarks (E003, E004). A secondary surgical removal was performed at the primary site with a 1 cm excision distance (E004). The patient has been followed for 30 months with CT/MRI scans, showing no sign of recurrence or other primary neuroendocrine tumor (E005).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with a 4 mm skin tumor under the left nipple, present for 5-6 years.
Histology showed a 4 mm dermal tumor with solid and organoid patterns, uniform cells, and a mitotic count of 8 per 2 mm2, without necrosis or mucin.

Immunohistochemistry was positive for synaptophysin, CD56, S-100, SOX-10, SATB2, ISLET-1, and dot-like pan cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), indicating neuroendocrine differentiation and supporting cutaneous origin.
Ki-67 index was up to 10%, consistent with a low-grade tumor.
Negative staining for Merkel Cell Polyomavirus (MCPyV) and CK20, ruling out Merkel cell carcinoma.
Negative staining for TTF-1 and CDX-2, and negative FDG-PET scan, making a metastatic neuroendocrine tumor less likely.
Secondary surgical removal of the primary site with a 1 cm excision distance, followed by 30 months of surveillance with no recurrence.

Negative immunohistochemical staining for Merkel Cell Polyomavirus (MCPyV) and CK20 (E002), which are typically positive in Merkel cell carcinoma.
